subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 26-year-old man is evaluated for a 10-year history of episodes of burning pain in the hands and feet that worsen with fever and exercise, and he has never sweated normally. Examination shows small red-purple macules around the umbilicus and scrotum. Urinalysis shows proteinuria.
question: Deficiency of which of the following enzymes is most likely responsible?
explanation_correct: Episodic burning pain in the hands and feet, angiokeratomas, and hypohidrosis form the early triad of Fabry disease, an X-linked recessive disorder. Alpha-galactosidase A deficiency leads to lysosomal accumulation of ceramide trihexoside (globotriaosylceramide) in skin, nerves, kidney, and heart. Later complications include progressive renal failure and cardiovascular disease, and recombinant alpha-galactosidase A is used for treatment.

explanation_incorrect.A: Arylsulfatase A deficiency causes metachromatic leukodystrophy with demyelination and ataxia, not angiokeratomas.
explanation_incorrect.B: Glucocerebrosidase deficiency causes Gaucher disease with splenomegaly, pancytopenia, and bone crises.
explanation_incorrect.C: Sphingomyelinase deficiency causes Niemann-Pick disease with hepatosplenomegaly and a cherry-red spot.
explanation_incorrect.E: Galactocerebrosidase deficiency causes Krabbe disease with globoid cells and peripheral neuropathy.

educationalObjective: Fabry disease, from alpha-galactosidase A deficiency, causes acroparesthesias, angiokeratomas, hypohidrosis, and later renal and cardiovascular disease.
